subject: Dedicated capacity commitment and tranche schedule for Atlas Labs Q3 rollout
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily@atlaslabs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@atlaslabs.com>, procurement@atlaslabs.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity request: Atlas Labs Q3 model rollout

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and latency numbers looked great. We're on an aggressive timeline to put our vision model into production for enterprise customers starting the first week of August (target GA 2027-08-02).

High-level ask: a dedicated pool to support inference at peak for the first 90 days post-GA. Engineering estimates we need about 35-50 A6000-equivalent GPUs sustained for inference (with short peaks up to ~80 for retraining/refresh windows). Core requirements: 99.9% availability SLA for inference endpoints, isolated compute (no multi-tenant sharing), and predictable burst capacity during weekly re-index windows.

We'd like a proposal with a tranche schedule and clear fallbacks if capacity is constrained. Pricing sensitivity matters — procurement needs an MSRP and a committed discount for a 12-month follow-on. Can you get us a sizing + commitment plan by EOD Monday so we can review with finance?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Head of ML Engineering, Atlas Labs

---
Attachment: design-diagram-v1.svg (image/svg)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@atlaslabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 13:50:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request: Atlas Labs Q3 model rollout

Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. I'm attaching an initial capacity proposal (capacity-proposal-v2.pdf) that outlines three tranche options:

- Option A (Conservative): Reserve 40 GPUs dedicated for 90 days with a guaranteed 6-GPU burst pool; strong SLA, higher discount threshold.
- Option B (Balanced): Reserve 30 GPUs with the ability to burst to 60 GPUs for up to 8 hours/week via our "burst lane" policy; medium discount.
- Option C (Cost-first): Reserve 20 GPUs + host routing fallback to our hosted fleet for spikes; lower commitment and price.

Key tradeoffs are described in the doc (latency/SLA vs unit economics). I've also attached an SOW template (SOW-Atlas-2027.docx) for procurement to review.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal sizing confirmation (we'll validate exact A6000-equivalent counts).
2) You pick a tranche option (A/B/C) and confirm whether you require strict isolation vs soft isolation with tenant-aware guarantees.
3) We lock a preliminary MOU and DocuSign (link below) to hold capacity while we finalize terms.

If you need to accelerate, we can provision a canary in late June (smaller pool) and then scale at GA.

I've looped in Rishi and Karthik on the capacity planning and trade-offs. Rishi — can you confirm whether the fleet can support Option A timing-wise without impacting committed enterprise customers next month?

Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request: Atlas Labs Q3 model rollout

Monica —

Thanks for the summary. Quick operational reality check: Q3 already has two near-committed reservations that overlap with Atlas's requested window — NOVA-331 (mid-market expansion) and a pre-committed research tranche for a partner pilot (starts 2027-07-20). If we accept Option A (40 GPUs) for Atlas starting 2027-07-25, we will need to re-tranche one of the other commitments or apply stricter burst controls.

Some thoughts:
- We can support a time-limited Option A if Atlas agrees to a staged start (20 GPUs day-one; add +10 after 2 weeks; full 40 by week 6) and signs a firm MOU that includes rollback windows and usage caps.
- Alternatively, offer Option B with guaranteed 30 GPUs and a contractual burst cap (e.g., 60 GPUs for up to 6 hours/week) and higher overage rates. That preserves headroom for NOVA-331.
- Reserve a small canary cluster (4 GPUs) in late June to validate perf; that buys us telemetry before GA.

If we push for Option A flat-start, we should prepare an escalation memo for the Capacity Steering Committee and surface the customer impact (what we would deprioritize). Laura — please prepare a short impact matrix if we go down that route.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Capacity & Infrastructure

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request: Atlas Labs Q3 model rollout

Folks —

Operational recommendation based on current fleet forecasts:

1) Offer Atlas Option B as the default commercial path: 30 GPUs reserved, burst lane up to 60 GPUs (6 hours/week), price at "mid-commit" tier. This limits impact on NOVA-331 and partner pilot.

2) For customers who need strict isolation (Option A), tie flat-start availability to either (a) shifting NOVA-331 start by 3 weeks or (b) a short-term capacity purchase from our spot partners (at higher cost) for the initial month. Both require executive sign-off.

3) Implement a short-lived (6-week) telemetry canary starting 2027-06-22 with 4 GPUs to gather real traffic profiles. If telemetry matches Atlas estimates, we accelerate tranche increases.

4) Prepare a formal escalation pack (1-pager) if Atlas chooses Option A; include clear customer impact and suggested mitigation (graceful degradation: route noncritical endpoints to hosted).

If we need to escalate, I recommend a Thursday morning capacity sync with Rishi, Laura, Monica, and Engineering Ops.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Redwood Dedicated

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:00:00 -0400
Subject: Atlas Labs — next steps on tranche selection and MOU

Emily / Procurement —

Following internal capacity review, Redwood's operational recommendation is to proceed with Option B (30 GPU reserved tranche + burst lane to 60 GPUs for up to 6 hours/week). This preserves predictability for your GA while allowing us to honor other near-committed customers.

If Atlas requires strict isolation (Option A), we can provide a flat-start 40 GPU reservation but would need one of the following before we lock it:
- Approval to shift NOVA-331 by 3 weeks (internal impact) OR
- A one-month temporary capacity uplift purchased at the premium "spot partner" rate (we'd pass through the cost) AND
- A signed short-form MOU with explicit rollback windows.

Next steps I ask of you today:
1) Confirm which option you prefer (A/B/C) and whether you need strict isolation.
2) For Option B: sign the MOU placeholder here so we can provision the initial tranche and set the canary schedule. DocuSign link: https://redwood.app/docusign/ATL-4523-sign
3) For Option A: let me know if procurement can accept the premium uplift for month 1 or if you'd prefer we escalate internally.

I'll keep you posted on the canary timing (target 2027-06-22). Rishi/Karthik/Laura — please surface the impact pack if Atlas asks for Option A so we can escalate to the Capacity Steering Committee.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the options.

Monica
